title: Technical Test 1 — Electrical
blurb: Power path, standby generation, UPS and batteries, redundancy, fundamentals and safety.

questions.q: In the normal AWS power path, what sits between the main switchgear and the UPS?
choices: The rPDU
The automatic transfer switch (ATS)
The busway tap box
The server power supply
questions.why: Utility → transformer (MV to 480V) → main switchgear → ATS → UPS → PDU (480V to 208/120V) → busway/tap box → rPDU → server supply.

questions.q: Medium voltage (MV) distribution is roughly what range?
choices: 12kV–35kV
69kV–345kV
questions.why: HV is transmission-level, MV is distribution at roughly 12–35kV, LV is 480V and below inside the building.

questions.q: Where does the second step-down happen and to what voltage?
choices: At the ATS, 480V to 277V
At the UPS, 480V to 240V
At the PDU, 480V to 208/120V
At the rPDU, 208V to 120V
questions.why: The utility transformer drops MV to 480V; the PDU drops 480V to 208/120V for the racks.

questions.q: How does a transformer change voltage?
choices: Through magnetic coupling between windings, with no direct electrical connection
By rectifying and re-inverting the waveform
By mechanically switching taps under load
By resistive voltage division
questions.why: Magnetic coupling between two circuits. Step-down trades voltage for current. No moving parts and no direct connection between windings.

questions.q: Which best describes switchgear?
choices: The rack-level power strip servers plug into
The assembly of breakers, disconnects, protective relays and busbars that distributes and protects main power
A device that converts AC to DC for battery charging
Overhead bus-bar distribution running above the rows
questions.why: Switchgear is where large-scale switching and fault protection happens.

questions.q: What is the difference between a PDU and an rPDU?
choices: They are the same thing, different vendors
The PDU is floor-level and transforms/distributes; the rPDU is the strip in the rack servers plug into
The rPDU transforms 480V down; the PDU only monitors
The PDU is DC and the rPDU is AC
questions.why: PDU = floor unit doing transformation and branch distribution. rPDU = in-rack power strip.

questions.q: What is a tap box?
choices: A junction box where conductors are spliced inside a wall
The point where a circuit is tapped off an overhead busway to feed a rack without cutting conductors
A metering enclosure on the utility side
A terminal block inside the PDU
questions.why: Busway is overhead bus-bar distribution; the tap box is how you pull a circuit off it for a rack.

questions.q: Why does current balance across sources matter at the rack?
choices: Unbalanced load damages the server power supplies
Racks are dual-fed; if one side carries most of the load and fails, the other may not be able to pick up the whole load
It keeps the neutral conductor from carrying current
Balance is only a metering concern, not an operational one
questions.why: Dual-fed racks: an unbalanced pair means one source may be overloaded while the other is light, defeating the redundancy.

questions.q: In a utility loss, what carries the critical load first?
choices: The generator, within about two seconds
The UPS, instantly, off battery
The ATS, by bridging both sources
The PDU capacitor bank
questions.why: The UPS picks up instantly so servers see no interruption; the generator takes seconds to start and stabilize before the ATS transfers.

questions.q: Why aren't a UPS and generator interchangeable?
choices: The UPS is instant but only lasts minutes; the generator takes seconds to start but runs indefinitely
The generator is instant but low-capacity; the UPS is slow but high-capacity
The UPS handles mechanical load and the generator handles IT load
They are interchangeable in a 2N design
questions.why: The UPS bridges the gap until the generator is stable and carrying the load.

questions.q: What does an ATS monitor on the normal source?
choices: Current and power factor
Voltage and frequency
Harmonic distortion and phase rotation only
Ground fault current
questions.why: On loss or out-of-tolerance voltage/frequency it signals the generator to start and transfers once the alternate source is stable.

questions.q: What distinguishes closed transition from open transition transfer?
choices: Closed transition breaks before making, creating a dead interval
Closed transition briefly parallels both sources so the load never loses power, and requires synchronized sources
Closed transition can only be done manually
Closed transition transfers only the mechanical load
questions.why: Open transition = break-before-make with a brief dead interval. Closed = momentary paralleling, requires synchronization.

questions.q: Why is there a time delay on retransfer back to utility?
choices: To let the generator reach full operating temperature
To confirm utility is genuinely stable and not flickering, preventing repeated transfers
To allow the UPS batteries to fully recharge first
It is a code requirement with no operational purpose
questions.why: It prevents the ATS from bouncing back and forth on an unstable utility source.

questions.q: Why does a generator run a cooldown period after retransfer?
choices: To burn off unburned fuel in the exhaust
To let the engine cool gradually — an immediate hot shutdown causes thermal stress and shortens engine life
To recharge the starting batteries
To verify the ATS transferred correctly
questions.why: It runs unloaded for a period so the engine cools down gradually.

questions.q: A generator cranks but won't start. Which check is most likely to be skipped and most likely to be the cause?
choices: Testing batteries under crank load rather than at resting voltage
Checking the coolant level
Checking the air filter restriction gauge
Checking the alternator output voltage
questions.why: Also check fuel supply/valves, filters and water separator, air in the fuel system, stored controller faults, E-stop and safety shutdowns.

questions.q: The generator starts but will not take load. What is the most relevant first check?
choices: Oil level and oil pressure
Whether the ATS is seeing correct voltage and frequency from the generator, plus ATS control power and the generator breaker
Fuel polishing records
Block heater operation
questions.why: Then look at the voltage regulator and governor, and whether the set is actually reaching rated voltage and frequency.

questions.q: Why are starting batteries the most common generator failure point?
choices: They are undersized by most manufacturers
They sit idle at float, degrade silently, and can read fine at rest yet collapse under crank load
They are exposed to engine vibration
They discharge during weekly exercise runs
questions.why: Failure only shows up under starting current, which is why load-based battery testing matters.

questions.q: What is wet stacking?
choices: Water accumulating in the fuel tank from condensation
Unburned fuel accumulating in the exhaust when a diesel runs at light load for extended periods
Coolant leaking into the cylinders
Oil carryover into the turbocharger at high load
questions.why: Prevented by periodic loaded operation — which is one reason load bank testing exists.

questions.q: Why isn't a no-load exercise run a substitute for a load bank test?
choices: A no-load run doesn't prove rated capacity and doesn't load the diesel enough to prevent wet stacking
No-load runs void the manufacturer warranty
No-load runs cannot be logged in the BMS
A no-load run overheats the alternator
questions.why: Load banking applies an artificial load to prove the unit can actually carry rated capacity.

questions.q: What is a DRUPS?
choices: A dual-redundant UPS with two battery strings
A diesel rotary UPS using flywheel rotational energy to bridge the gap while the engine starts
A DC rectifier unit for battery plant supply
A distributed redundant power system across two utility feeds
questions.why: It's an alternative to a battery UPS — stored rotational energy carries the load until the diesel picks up.

questions.q: In a UPS, what does the rectifier do?
choices: Converts DC from the battery back to AC for the load
Converts incoming AC to DC
Routes load around the UPS on a fault
Regulates output frequency to match the bypass source
questions.why: Rectifier AC→DC, battery stores DC, inverter DC→clean AC, static bypass is the automatic fault path, maintenance bypass is the manual service path.

questions.q: What does double conversion accomplish?
choices: It doubles the runtime of the battery string
Power always flows rectifier-then-inverter, so the load is fully isolated from utility sags, surges and frequency variation
It converts three-phase to single-phase for rack distribution
It allows the UPS to run without batteries
questions.why: The output is regenerated clean rather than merely filtered.

questions.q: Static bypass versus maintenance bypass:
choices: Static is manual and used for service; maintenance is automatic on a fault
Static is automatic and instantaneous on a UPS fault; maintenance is a manual switch letting techs work on the UPS with load still energized
Both are automatic; they differ only in speed
Maintenance bypass drops the load briefly by design
questions.why: Static protects the load automatically. Maintenance bypass is a deliberate operator action.

questions.q: How long is a data center UPS typically designed to carry the load?
choices: About 5 to 15 minutes
About 60 to 90 minutes
About 4 hours
Long enough to ride through a typical multi-hour outage
questions.why: It only has to bridge until the generator picks up.

questions.q: What does specific gravity tell you about a flooded cell?
choices: Terminal torque adequacy
State of charge and cell health — a cell reading low relative to its neighbors is failing
Internal resistance at full discharge
Electrolyte temperature
questions.why: It's the density of the electrolyte relative to water, measured with a hydrometer.

questions.q: Why does a battery room need ventilation?
choices: To remove sulfuric acid vapor, which is corrosive
Charging lead-acid batteries produce hydrogen, which is explosive at concentration
To keep the room above the minimum rated temperature
To prevent dust accumulation on terminals
questions.why: Ventilation keeps hydrogen below dangerous levels. It's also why battery rooms are a fire and explosion concern.

questions.q: How does temperature affect battery plant?
choices: High temperature increases capacity; low temperature is harmless
High temperature accelerates degradation and shortens life; low temperature reduces available capacity
Temperature only matters for VRLA, not flooded cells
Batteries are rated at 100°F, so warmer rooms are preferred
questions.why: Batteries are rated at a specific temperature, typically 77°F.

questions.q: Float charge versus equalize charge:
choices: Float is a periodic high-voltage charge; equalize is continuous
Float is a continuous low-level charge keeping the battery topped off; equalize is a controlled higher-voltage charge to bring cells back into balance
Float applies only to VRLA; equalize applies only to flooded
They are two names for the same charging mode
questions.why: Float prevents overcharge during standby; equalize corrects cell imbalance.

questions.q: Why is breaker operation on a UPS handled so carefully?
choices: Breaker arcing damages the static switch
Wrong breaker or wrong order drops the critical load — you transfer to bypass before opening the UPS, not after
UPS breakers are rated for a limited number of operations
The inverter cannot restart once tripped
questions.why: Sequence is the whole point. This is a classic interview probe on procedural discipline.

questions.q: Which definition is correct?
choices: N+1 means a fully duplicated system
2N means one spare unit beyond requirement
N is exactly the capacity required; N+1 is one spare beyond that; 2N is fully duplicated; 2N+1 is duplicated plus a spare
2N+1 means two spares beyond requirement
questions.why: Know these cold — they come up in almost every EOT interview.

questions.q: Concurrent maintainability means:
choices: The facility survives an unplanned equipment failure without dropping load
Any single piece of equipment can be removed from service for maintenance without dropping the critical load
Maintenance can be performed by multiple crews at once
Two systems can be maintained on the same schedule
questions.why: That's planned work. Fault tolerance is the unplanned-failure equivalent.

questions.q: A target of 99.9999% uptime corresponds to roughly what downtime per year?
choices: About 30 seconds
About 5 minutes
About 52 minutes
About 8 hours
questions.why: Six nines is roughly 30 seconds annually — which is why single points of failure are designed out.

questions.q: PUE is defined as:
choices: IT equipment power divided by total facility power
Total facility power divided by IT equipment power, with cooling the main thing driving it up
Cooling power divided by IT power
Water consumed per unit of IT energy
questions.why: 1.0 is theoretically perfect. WUE is the water metric, and evaporative cooling trades one against the other.

questions.q: Which system monitors breaker status, metering, power quality and electrical alarms?
choices: BMS
EPMS
SCADA-lite
The rPDU controller
questions.why: EPMS = electrical plant. BMS = mechanical: chillers, CRAHs, pumps, temperature, humidity, airflow.

questions.q: Why do rounds still matter when you have a BMS?
choices: Rounds are a regulatory requirement with no operational value
Physical rounds catch what sensors miss — leaks, noises, smells, corrosion, loose connections, heat
The BMS only logs data hourly
Rounds are how the BMS is calibrated
questions.why: Instrumentation doesn't see everything. This is a strong answer to give in an interview.

questions.q: A meter reading disagrees with what you physically observe. What's the right move?
choices: Trust the instrument — it's calibrated
Trust your eyes and log the meter as faulty
Investigate and verify with a second method; a faulty sensor and a real fault look identical on a screen
Reset the sensor and re-read
questions.why: Assuming either one is right without verification is the mistake.

questions.q: The three-phase power formula is:
choices: P = V × I
P = √3 × V × I × power factor
P = I² × R × 3
questions.why: Ohm's Law is V = I × R; single-phase power is P = V × I.

questions.q: In a wye system, the relationship between line and phase voltage is:
choices: Line = phase
Line = √3 × phase, which is why 277V phase-to-neutral gives 480V phase-to-phase
Line = 2 × phase
Phase = √3 × line
questions.why: Same relationship gives 120V/208V.

questions.q: Why is three-phase used for large loads?
choices: It is safer at high voltage than single-phase
More power with less conductor material, constant rather than pulsing power delivery, and efficient motor starting and running
It eliminates the need for a neutral conductor
It produces a higher power factor automatically
questions.why: Constant power delivery is the key motor advantage.

questions.q: Poor power factor means:
choices: Voltage is below nominal at the load
Current is flowing that does no useful work, increasing losses and utility cost
The waveform contains excessive harmonics
The load is drawing more real power than rated
questions.why: Power factor is the ratio of real power to apparent power.

questions.q: What actually clears a ground fault?
choices: The earth connection at the ground rod
The bonding path back to the source — earth is a poor conductor and won't pass enough current to trip a breaker
The ground fault relay's shunt trip alone
The neutral-to-ground bond at the load
questions.why: This is the single most commonly missed electrical concept. Grounding is a reference to earth; bonding provides the fault-return path.

questions.q: Which standard governs arc flash boundaries, PPE categories and energized work permits?
choices: NFPA 70 (NEC)
NFPA 70E
NFPA 72
NFPA 25
questions.why: NFPA 70E is electrical safety in the workplace. The NEC (NFPA 70) governs installation.

questions.q: Which LOTO step is most commonly skipped?
choices: Notifying affected personnel
Applying the tag alongside the lock
Verification — testing for zero energy and proving the meter works before and after on a known live source
Releasing stored energy
questions.why: Full sequence: identify sources, notify, shut down and isolate, lock and tag, release stored energy, verify zero energy, then work.

questions.q: The two trip mechanisms in a typical molded case breaker are:
choices: Thermal (bimetallic, sustained overload) and magnetic (instantaneous, high short-circuit current)
Thermal and electronic ground fault
Magnetic and differential
Shunt trip and undervoltage release
questions.why: Fuses sacrifice themselves and must be replaced, but are typically faster on high fault currents.

questions.q: Coordination in a protective scheme means:
choices: All devices trip simultaneously to guarantee isolation
The device closest to the fault trips first, isolating the smallest possible section
Upstream devices trip first to protect downstream equipment
Breakers and fuses are matched by manufacturer
questions.why: Poor coordination drops far more load than necessary.

questions.q: Conductor sizing depends on more than amperage because of:
choices: Conductor color coding and labeling requirements
Insulation temperature rating, ambient temperature, bundling of current-carrying conductors, and voltage drop over distance
Breaker manufacturer specifications
The power factor of the connected load
questions.why: Voltage drop is generally kept within 3% on branch circuits.

questions.q: How does a VFD control motor speed?
choices: By varying the voltage applied to the stator
By rectifying AC to DC then inverting back to AC at a controlled frequency — motor speed follows frequency
By switching pole configuration in the motor windings
By mechanically varying the load through a coupling
questions.why: Speed follows frequency, so pumps and fans run only as hard as needed.

questions.q: Why do VFDs save so much energy on pumps and fans?
choices: They eliminate inrush current entirely
Affinity laws — power varies roughly with the cube of speed, so 80% speed uses roughly half the power
They correct power factor to unity
They allow the motor to run on single-phase supply
questions.why: The cube relationship is why partial-speed operation is such a large win.

questions.q: Why do data centers care about harmonics?
choices: They reduce the available fault current at the switchboard
Distortion from non-linear loads like rectifiers and drives causes overheating in transformers and neutrals and can trip equipment
They lower the frequency seen by the ATS
They only affect the generator, not the utility feed
questions.why: Non-linear loads are everywhere in a data center, which makes this a live concern.

questions.q: Why is load pickup staggered when a generator starts?
choices: To give the ATS time to verify frequency on each step
Bringing all loads on at once causes an inrush spike that can overload the generator and cause it to trip or stall
To reduce harmonic distortion during transfer
To keep the UPS from returning to float too quickly
questions.why: Load management modules bring load on in steps. Inrush is many times running current for motors and transformers.
